label: CUDA-graphed decode
mechanism: batched decode step captured into per-device CUDA graphs — static buffers, B padded to max_batch, monotone 512-bucket key length, one argmax readback
hypothesis: Adjudicated attack (a) from the exp-0011 in-situ profile row (insitu_phase_exp0011_2026-07-30.log: dec_enq 107.1 s of dec_wall 108.4 s over 256 steps at ~64 rows — host enqueue = 98.8% of decode-step wall): delete the per-step host dispatch (~6k eager Python/torch/Triton enqueues over the 66-layer pooled traversal) by capturing the step into per-device CUDA graphs replayed on static buffers. Staticization: B padded to max_batch via a dedicated pool scratch slot (identically-configured dead rows so colliding scratch writes carry identical bytes; kv.py +1 row/page), global key length padded to a monotone 512-bucket high-water L_pad (recapture <= 32/lifetime; only the current bucket ever replays after a new capture, keeping shared per-device graph pools in capture order), layer-2's bf16 expert reference loop as an eager island on LIVE rows only (dead rows in its per-hit-expert GEMM batches would couple live-token bits to scratch history through row counts), bincount -> searchsorted in moe_experts_packed (bit-identical integer offsets; bincount's data-dependent output size is a hidden device sync that invalidates capture), page allocation hoisted to a page-boundary host check, and the 64 per-row argmax .item() syncs collapsed to ONE batched argmax readback. MEASURED (in-process A/B, one resident load, 64 reqs, /workspace/logs/t_graph_ab_exp0012_2026-07-30.log): graph run1 == run2 BITWISE across a mid-run 512->1024 bucket recapture (the t_b3-adapted determinism arm); warm graphed step 473.0 ms vs eager 476.6 ms (+0.76% at ISL 220-500). The premise was WRONG in an instructive way: exp-0011's host-enqueue share measured the host WALL, not GPU idleness — the kernel profile of the graphed step (t_graph_profile_exp0012_2026-07-30.log, ISL~700-772, 459.7 ms/step CUDA total) shows the step was ALREADY GPU-bound at near-parity with dispatch: _gate_up_silu 184.9 + _down_scale 81.5 = 266.4 ms/step (58%) in the grouped packed-NVFP4 GEMMs (dequant-ALU-bound at M~1-2 rows per hit expert, ~5.7x off the ~47 ms/step weight-traffic roofline) plus ~128 ms/step (28%) of matmul-contiguous direct_copy on the pooled attention K/V gathers (260 copies/step). Bench prediction is therefore ~flat; the row locks in the dispatch floor — the substrate every kernel-side win needs so host cost cannot re-emerge as kernels shrink (at 200 ms/step of GPU the eager path's ~450 ms host wall would dominate; the graphed path's host cost is ~the island only) — and its kernel table adjudicates the ranked-next attacks: (1) decode-shape grouped NVFP4 GEMM (dequant-once staging or the CUDA/CUTLASS native-FP4-MMA port, D5 roadmap / exp-0010 DEADENDS) worth up to ~220 ms/step, (2) copy-free two-shape attention with fused rel-bias (attack #5) worth up to ~120 ms/step.
predicted_delta: +0.0 to +1.0% tok/s decode_heavy (69.5-70.7 vs best 70.0; merge bar 70.21) — likely REJECTED like warmup-0000/exp-0011; every measured attempt is chartable data. Deliverables either way: the dispatch-floor substrate on this branch's lineage and the graphed-step kernel table above, which the next iteration's spec must cite.
